name: Gardenfall Binary

stars.name: Gardenfall A
stars.notes: Bright primary star, slightly more luminous than Sol, drives robust photosynthetic activity on inner worlds

stars.name: Gardenfall B
stars.notes: Companion star in a wide 180 AU orbit, hosts its own stable planetary system in the outer region

planets.name: Sunforge
planets.notes: Innermost world around Gardenfall A. Extreme solar radiation has vitrified its surface into natural glass plains.

planets.name: Elysara
planets.notes: Primary garden world, Earth-like with four continents and rich biodiversity. Population 5.1 billion. Towering deciduous forests turn golden-red in autumn cycles visible from orbit.

planets.name: Aquaverde
planets.notes: Warm ocean world with extensive shallow seas and coral megastructures. Population 2.3 billion in floating city-states. Indigenous aquatic life includes photosynthetic jellyfish colonies.

planets.name: Thornhaven
planets.notes: Cool temperate world at the habitable zone's edge, covered in thorny scrublands and hardy forests. Population 340 million, primarily agricultural settlements.

planets.name: Gardenfall Magnus
planets.notes: Massive jovian with distinctive green-banded atmosphere from phosphine compounds. Four large moons host research facilities.

planets.name: Briarfrost
planets.notes: Orbits Gardenfall B. Frozen world with cryovolcanic activity and subsurface liquid water ocean.

planets.name: Dimreach
planets.notes: Orbits Gardenfall B. Airless rock used as a fuel depot and waystation for traffic between the two stellar subsystems.

planets.name: Farhallow
planets.notes: Outermost world orbiting Gardenfall B. Nitrogen ice surface with trace organic compounds detected in impact craters.

anomalies.name: The Verdant Drift
anomalies.location: Lagrange point between Gardenfall A and B subsystems
anomalies.notes: A diffuse cloud of extremophilic microorganisms surviving in the vacuum between the two stars. Origin unknown—possibly ejected from one of the living worlds by ancient impacts.

asteroid_belts.name: The Garden Wall
asteroid_belts.notes: Thick asteroid belt rich in metals and silicates. Major mining operations fuel the system's industrial needs while keeping extraction away from inhabited worlds.

asteroid_belts.name: B-Ring
asteroid_belts.location: Outer region of Gardenfall B subsystem
asteroid_belts.notes: Thin icy debris ring around the secondary star system. Comet captures are frequent.

stations.name: Gardenfall Central
stations.notes: Massive trade hub handling commerce for three inhabited worlds. Features extensive biodome sections growing plants from all three biospheres.

stations.name: Coralspire Platform
stations.notes: Combined trade and research station. Manages Aquaverde's floating city logistics and coordinates marine conservation enforcement.

stations.name: Thornhaven Dock
stations.notes: Agricultural export hub shipping grain, timber, and bioengineered crop strains to colonies across the sector.

stations.name: Bridgepoint
stations.location: Midpoint between Gardenfall A and B subsystems
stations.notes: Transit station for traffic crossing between the two stellar subsystems. Also serves as the primary observation post for the Verdant Drift anomaly.

stations.name: Wall Forge
stations.notes: Industrial mining complex providing raw materials for system-wide construction. Strict waste protocols prevent contamination of inner worlds.

faction_control.notes: Federal democratic governance uniting three inhabited worlds. Each world maintains local autonomy within a shared ecological and defense framework.

history: First surveyed in 2238, the binary system's unusually wide stellar separation and multiple habitable worlds made it a priority colonization target. Settlement ships arrived in 2249.
The Gardenfall Commonwealth was formally established in 2272 after the three colony worlds negotiated a federal charter balancing development rights with conservation mandates.

Discovery of the Verdant Drift in 2291 sparked intense scientific debate about panspermia and the possibility that life in the system originated from spaceborne microorganisms rather than independent abiogenesis.
description: Gardenfall Binary is a system of extraordinary abundance. Two stars—one bright yellow-white, one warm orange—orbit each other at a distance wide enough to permit stable planetary systems around each. The primary harbors three inhabited worlds, each a garden in its own right: Elysara's forests blaze with seasonal color, Aquaverde's coral megastructures are visible from space, and Thornhaven's hardy scrublands feed millions through resilient agriculture. The secondary star hosts only frozen worlds, but even there, Briarfrost's subsurface ocean hints at the system's irrepressible tendency toward life.

With nearly eight billion inhabitants across three worlds, Gardenfall is one of the most populous life-bearing systems in known space. The Commonwealth's governance model is widely studied—three very different worlds with distinct cultures and economies cooperating under a shared charter that prioritizes both prosperity and preservation. Gardenfall Central station, with nearly a million residents, serves as the neutral ground where representatives meet, deals are brokered, and the system's considerable trade flows outward to dozens of neighboring systems.

The Verdant Drift remains the system's deepest mystery. Extremophilic organisms surviving in the hard vacuum between two stars should be impossible, yet they persist—a diffuse cloud of life clinging to existence in the most hostile environment imaginable. If these organisms are ancestral to life on the system's worlds, it would rewrite understanding of how biology spreads through space. Bridgepoint station's researchers have spent decades studying the Drift, and their findings grow more puzzling with each passing year. Life, it seems, finds a way in Gardenfall—whether anyone expects it to or not.
